nodes.description: Hemangioblastomas of the cerebellum are the most common CNS manifestation, occurring in 60-80% of VHL patients. These highly vascular tumors may cause symptoms through mass effect or associated cyst formation.

evidence.reference_title: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
evidence.snippet: HP:0006880 | Cerebellar hemangioblastoma | Frequent (79-30%)

nodes.description: PBRM1, BAP1 and SETD2 sit near VHL on chromosome 3p, so the loss of heterozygosity that supplies the somatic second hit typically removes them along with VHL. Their inactivation is a cooperating event in clear cell renal carcinoma rather than a consequence of pseudohypoxia, and which modifier is hit tracks with tumor behaviour: BAP1 loss with high-grade, sarcomatoid, poor-survival disease and PBRM1 loss with a more indolent course. This is a somatic co-driver layer observed mainly in sporadic clear cell renal carcinoma cohorts; inherited VHL-associated tumors carry fewer alterations overall, so the extent to which the same requirement holds in VHL disease is not settled.

evidence.reference_title: The genomic landscape of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma and its prognostic value: a comprehensive analysis of a large real-world clinico-genomic database.
evidence.snippet: The top 10 mutated genes were VHL (73.9%), PBRM1 (42.4%), SETD2 (25.3%), CDKN2A (20.0%), BAP1 (16.4%), CDKN2B (16.0%), KDM5C (14.5%), TP53 (12.9%), PTEN (11.7%), and TERT (9.2%).

evidence.reference_title: Emerging roles for the epigenetic modifiers PBRM1 SETD2 and BAP1 in clear cell renal cell carcinoma pathogenesis and prognosis beyond VHL.
evidence.snippet: PBRM1 loss (∼40%), a subunit of the SWI/SNF complex, is linked to a more indolent phenotype and potential sensitivity to antiangiogenic therapy as well as immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) resistance. SETD2 mutations (10–15%) cause genomic instability and are associated with aggressive features but may improve the ICI response. BAP1 mutation (10–15%) strongly predicts high-grade tumors, sarcomatoid differentiation, poor survival, and therapy resistance.

nodes.description: Clear cell RCC occurs in approximately 70% of VHL patients. Tumors are often bilateral and multifocal. Mean age of diagnosis is 39 years, compared to 62 years for sporadic RCC. Leading cause of mortality in VHL patients.

evidence.reference_title: Belzutifan for Renal Cell Carcinoma in von Hippel-Lindau Disease.
evidence.snippet: Patients with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease have a high incidence of renal cell carcinoma owing to VHL gene inactivation and constitutive activation of the transcription factor hypoxia-inducible factor 2α (HIF-2α).

nodes.description: Stabilized HIF-alpha (primarily HIF-2alpha in RCC) dimerizes with HIF-1beta (ARNT) and translocates to the nucleus where it activates transcription of hypoxia-responsive genes. This occurs constitutively regardless of oxygen levels, creating a pseudo-hypoxic state. The two alpha isoforms are not interchangeable here: HIF-2alpha is the oncogenic driver, and pharmacologic and genetic work in clear cell renal carcinoma places the tumor's dependency specifically on HIF-2 rather than on HIF-alpha generically.

evidence.reference_title: Up-regulation of hypoxia-inducible factors HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha under normoxic conditions in renal carcinoma cells by von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor gene loss of function.
evidence.snippet: in VHL deficient cell lines, both HIF-alpha subunits are constitutively expressed, whereas re-introduction of a functional VHL gene restores the instability of HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha proteins under normoxic conditions.

evidence.reference_title: HIF-2 Complex Dissociation, Target Inhibition, and Acquired Resistance with PT2385, a First-in-Class HIF-2 Inhibitor, in Patients with Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: Prolonged PT2385 treatment resulted in the acquisition of resistance, and we identified a gatekeeper mutation (G323E) in HIF2α, which interferes with drug binding and precluded HIF-2 complex dissociation.

nodes.description: Endolymphatic sac tumors are inner-ear neoplasms within the VHL tumor spectrum.

evidence.snippet: HP:0030393 | Endolymphatic sac tumor | Occasional (29-5%)

nodes.description: HIF activates transcription of genes including PDGF, TGF-alpha, EGFR, GLUT1, and glycolytic enzymes. This promotes cell proliferation, survival, and a shift toward glycolytic metabolism (Warburg effect) that supports tumor growth.

evidence.reference_title: von Hippel-Lindau disease-related neoplasia with an emphasis on renal manifestations.
evidence.snippet: immunohistochemical studies for markers such as paired box 8 (PAX-8), carbonic anhydrase 9 (CA9), and glucose transporter 1 (GLUT-1) have an important role in routine clinical practice and represent cost-effective diagnostic tools.

nodes.description: pVHL has activities beyond HIF-alpha ubiquitylation, including fibronectin and extracellular matrix assembly, primary cilium maintenance, and regulation of JAK/STAT signalling through SOCS proteins. Loss of these activities is a separate arm of VHL pathogenesis from pseudohypoxia. The evidence that it matters clinically comes from the genotype-phenotype boundary: the alleles that produce pheochromocytoma without hemangioblastoma or renal carcinoma (type 2C) still ubiquitylate HIF-alpha normally and still bind pVHL partners normally, so something other than HIF dysregulation must be driving chromaffin-cell transformation in those families. Which pVHL activity that is has not been established.

evidence.reference_title: Contrasting effects on HIF-1alpha regulation by disease-causing pVHL mutations correlate with patterns of tumourigenesis in von Hippel-Lindau disease.
evidence.snippet: Mutations associated with the PHE-only phenotype (type 2C) promoted HIF-alpha ubiquitylation in vitro and demonstrated wild-type binding patterns with pVHL interacting proteins, suggesting that loss of other pVHL functions are necessary for PHE susceptibility.

nodes.description: VHL protein (pVHL) functions as the substrate recognition component of an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that targets hydroxylated HIF-alpha subunits for proteasomal degradation under normoxic conditions. Loss of VHL function prevents HIF-alpha degradation, allowing HIF accumulation even in the presence of oxygen.

evidence.reference_title: The VHL tumor suppressor: master regulator of HIF.
evidence.snippet: The von-Hippel Lindau tumor suppressor (pVHL) is the substrate recognition component of an E3 ubiquitin ligase and functions as a master regulator of HIF activity by targeting the hydroxylated HIF-alpha subunit for ubiquitylation and rapid proteasomal degradation under normoxic conditions.

evidence.reference_title: von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor: not only HIF's executioner.
evidence.snippet: VHL tumor suppressor is a specific substrate-recognition component of the E3 ubiquitin complex, which regulates proteasomal degradation of the subunit of the hypoxia inducible transcription factor (HIF). Impaired VHL complex function leads to accumulation of HIF, overexpression of various HIF-induced gene products and formation of highly vascular neoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: Structural basis for the recognition of hydroxyproline in HIF-1 alpha by pVHL.
evidence.snippet: The crystal structure of a hydroxylated HIF-1 alpha peptide bound to VCB (pVHL, elongins C and B) and solution binding assays reveal a single, conserved hydroxyproline-binding pocket in pVHL.

nodes.description: Pancreatic cysts (serous cystadenomas) are common in VHL patients but are almost always benign. They are distinct from pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.

evidence.reference_title: von Hippel-Lindau disease-related neoplasia with an emphasis on renal manifestations.
evidence.snippet: Individuals with VHL disease develop numerous cysts and tumors involving multiple organs including the kidneys, central nervous system, endolymphatic sac, lungs, pancreatobiliary system, adrenal glands, epididymis, and/or broad ligament.

nodes.description: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors occur in 5-17% of VHL patients. Most are nonfunctional. The main concern is metastatic potential, though most are indolent. Size-based surveillance guides management.

evidence.reference_title: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
evidence.snippet: HP:0030405 | Pancreatic endocrine tumor | Occasional (29-5%)

nodes.description: Pheochromocytomas occur in 10-20% of VHL patients overall but are more common in Type 2 families (up to 60%). Often bilateral and may occur at young ages. Screening by plasma or urine metanephrines is recommended.

evidence.reference_title: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
evidence.snippet: pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma.

nodes.description: Multiple renal cysts are common in VHL patients and may precede RCC development. Some cysts contain foci of clear cell RCC. Surveillance imaging monitors for solid enhancing components.

nodes.description: Retinal hemangioblastomas (also called retinal capillary hemangiomas) occur in 25-60% of VHL patients and may be the presenting manifestation. They can cause vision loss through exudation, hemorrhage, or retinal detachment.

evidence.reference_title: Von Hippel-Lindau disease
evidence.snippet: HP:0009711 | Retinal capillary hemangioma | Frequent (79-30%)

nodes.description: The combination of increased angiogenesis, growth factor signaling, and metabolic reprogramming creates a permissive environment for tumor development. Different tissues show variable susceptibility, explaining the characteristic tumor spectrum of VHL disease including RCC, hemangioblastomas, and pheochromocytomas.

evidence.reference_title: The VHL tumor suppressor: master regulator of HIF.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in pVHL can be found in familial and sporadic hemangioblastomas, clear cell carcinomas of the kidney, pheochromocytomas and inherited forms of erythrocytosis, illustrating the importance of disrupted molecular oxygen sensing in the pathogenesis of these diseases.

evidence.reference_title: von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor: not only HIF's executioner.
evidence.snippet: Loss of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) protein function results in an autosomal-dominant cancer syndrome known as VHL disease, which manifests as angiomas of the retina, hemangioblastomas of the central nervous system, renal clear-cell carcinomas and pheochromocytomas.

nodes.description: VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor) is a direct HIF target gene. Constitutive HIF activation leads to chronic VEGF overexpression, driving extensive tumor angiogenesis. This explains the highly vascular nature of VHL-associated tumors, particularly hemangioblastomas and clear cell RCC.

biological_processes: vascular endothelial growth factor signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: Up-regulation of hypoxia-inducible factors HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha under normoxic conditions in renal carcinoma cells by von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor gene loss of function.
evidence.snippet: In a previous study of hemangioblastomas, the most frequent manifestation of hereditary von Hippel-Lindau disease (VHL), we found elevated levels of vascular endothelial growth factor and HIF-2alpha mRNA in stromal cells of the tumors.

evidence.reference_title: Up-regulation of hypoxia-inducible factors HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha under normoxic conditions in renal carcinoma cells by von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor gene loss of function.
evidence.snippet: The data presented here provide evidence for a role of the VHL protein in regulation of angiogenesis and erythropoiesis mediated by the HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Coexpression of erythropoietin and vascular endothelial growth factor in nervous system tumors associated with von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor gene loss of function.
evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, we observed Epo mRNA expression in all hemangioblastoma specimens analyzed, but in none of four glioblastomas. In contrast, VEGF mRNA was expressed in all hemangioblastomas and all glioblastomas. In situ hybridization revealed neoplastic stromal cells as Epo- and VEGF-producing cells in hemangioblastomas.

nodes.description: Germline heterozygous VHL mutations result in one functional allele. Somatic loss or mutation of the remaining wild-type allele (second hit) eliminates VHL function, initiating tumorigenesis. This follows Knudson's two-hit hypothesis for tumor suppressor gene inactivation.

evidence.reference_title: von Hippel-Lindau disease-related neoplasia with an emphasis on renal manifestations.
evidence.snippet: von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease is characterized by biallelic inactivation of the VHL gene leading to abnormal or absent VHL protein function, and constitutive activation of hypoxia-inducible factors (HIF) that leads to pro-tumorigenic signaling.
